book: Pirkei Avot — Ethics of the Fathers

1: Moses received the Torah at Sinai and handed it down to Joshua; Joshua to the elders; the elders to the prophets; and the prophets handed it down to the men of the Great Assembly. They said three things: Be deliberate in judgement, raise up many disciples, and make a fence around the Torah.
Hillel said: Be of the disciples of Aaron — loving peace and pursuing peace, loving your fellow creatures and drawing them near to the Torah.
He used to say: He who makes his name great causes his name to be destroyed; he who does not add to his learning causes it to be lost; and he who does not serve is worthy of death.
He used to say: If I am not for myself, who is for me? And if I am only for myself, what am I? And if not now — when?
Shammai said: Make your Torah a fixed habit; say little and do much; and receive every person with a cheerful face.
2: He used to say: Do not be sure of yourself until the day you die; do not judge your fellow until you have reached his place; and say not of a matter that is impossible, 'It cannot be understood,' for in the end it may be understood.
Rabbi Eliezer said: Let the honour of your friend be as dear to you as your own; do not let yourself be easily provoked to anger; and repent one day before your death.
Rabbi Tarfon said: The day is short, the task is great, the labourers are idle, the wage is abundant, and the Master of the house is urgent.

It is not your duty to finish the work, but neither are you free to desist from it. If you have studied much Torah, you will be given abundant reward — and your Employer is faithful to pay the wage of your labour. But know that the reward of the righteous is in the world to come.
He used to say: Beloved are human beings, for they were created in the image of God; doubly beloved, for it was made known to them that they were created in His image.
3: Reflect upon three things and you will not come to sin: know from where you came, and where you are going, and before whom you are destined to give account and reckoning. From where do you come? From a drop in the darkness. Where are you going? To a place of dust and worms. Before whom must you give account? Before the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.

Beloved are Israel, for to them was given the precious instrument — the Torah. Beloved is man, for he was created in the image of God. Everything is foreseen, yet freedom of choice is given; the world is judged with goodness, and all is according to the preponderance of works.
He who occupies himself with the study of Torah in poverty will in the end fulfil it in wealth; and he who neglects the Torah in wealth will in the end fulfil his neglect in poverty.

He who possesses these three traits is among the disciples of Abraham our father, and he who possesses the three opposite traits is among the disciples of Balaam the wicked. The disciples of Abraham have a good eye, a humble spirit, and a lowly soul.
[Avot 3:24 — Rabbi Eliezer ha-Kappar on small things]

Let not the contempt of anything be light in your eyes, nor let your table be a place of mockery. Run to a light commandment as to a weighty one, and flee from transgression; for one commandment leads to another, and one transgression leads to another.
